reason: The barbell is doing exactly what it was rebuilt to do and the week confirmed the regime it was built for: the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with 16 of 18 participants pencilling in at least one more, the 10-year printed 5.00% on Friday, Brent is holding above $100 on the Iran/Hormuz shock, and equity funds saw a fourth straight week of outflows. Against that backdrop the book is +3.55% since inception versus SPY +1.71%, with a max drawdown under 3%, and every leg of the 2026-09-16 fill except BRK-B is green (NVDA +3.9%, AVGO +5.3%, GLD +2.4%, MRK +1.4%, JNJ +1.0%, ANET +0.9%, XLE +0.4%). The one thing that tested the aggressive sleeve, the 14-15 September chip selloff after the Amodei/Altman/Musk calls to slow frontier development that knocked the SOX down ~6%, has already been absorbed: the AI-infra legs recovered to new leg highs by Friday as XLK led the tape +2.2%, and the -18% stops on NVDA/AVGO/ANET remain the designed answer if Micron's report next week reopens the capex-digestion fear. BRK-B is -1.9% on Buffett handing the chairmanship to Howard Buffett, which is a long-telegraphed governance headline, not an earnings or balance-sheet event, and Q2 revenue was +10% with earnings more than doubled, so I keep the ballast. The 40% cash earning 4% APY is not idle in a hiking cycle with a 5% ten-year; it is the rate-resilient half of the barbell and is now paid better than it was a month ago. A full replacement would cost real basis points to arrive at essentially the same book. Nothing in the tape argues for more risk (outflows, oil, hawkish dots) or for less (AI sleeve intact, stops in place), so holding beats trading.
